headline: Oxford Don Spins Fantastical Tale for Three Girls on the Thames
dispatch: On the afternoon of July 4, Oxford lecturer Charles Dodgson rowed three young sisters up the Thames from Folly Bridge toward Godstow, entertaining them with an improvised tale of a girl who tumbles down a rabbit hole into a land of impossible creatures. The eldest, Alice Liddell, pleaded that he write it down. The story told that afternoon will become Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.
answer: Lewis Carroll tells Alice Liddell the Wonderland story, 1862
